title: Clarifying customer and writer questions
summary: This topic is dominated by procedural fragments where writers or customers ask follow-up questions about vehicle features, setup, charging, connectivity, or issue details, with little direct sentiment content.

positive.summary: Positive examples reflect interest in usability or favorable impressions when asking about what makes the vehicle good or whether a system is comfortable and straightforward to use.

negative.summary: The negative example concerns a writer asking the customer to be present at the vehicle so an issue could be observed, indicating inconvenience around troubleshooting.

undetermined.summary: Undetermined examples are mainly information-gathering questions about chargers, screen behavior, account setup, connectivity, size, and requests for more detail without clear praise or complaint.

limitations: Most sampled fragments are undetermined because they capture questions rather than outcomes or evaluations.
The topic mixes several unrelated subjects, including charging, infotainment, connectivity, vehicle size, and general troubleshooting prompts.
Known-sentiment examples are sparse, so sentiment-specific conclusions are limited.
